questions.stem: What is the conjugate of the binomial (3x - 4)?
questions.solution: The conjugate of a binomial (a - b) is obtained by changing the sign between the two terms, so the conjugate of (3x - 4) is (-3x + 4).
questions.explanation: Conjugates are pairs of binomials that differ only in the sign between their terms.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to reverse both signs, which results in choice A, but this is not the correct conjugate.

questions.stem: Find the conjugate pair of the binomial (2 - √5).
questions.solution: The conjugate of a binomial with a radical (a - b√c) is (a + b√c), so the conjugate pair is (2 - √5) and (2 + √5).
questions.explanation: When dealing with radicals, only the term inside the square root changes sign.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to reverse both terms, which results in choice B, but this does not form a conjugate pair.

questions.explanation: Complex conjugates involve swapping the sign of the imaginary component.
